title: Graceful Retry Window and Penalty Crediting Protocol for Duplicate Usage Suppression
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: At-least-once ingestion semantics plus client-side aggressive retries and transient rate-limiting lead to duplicate billing and inflated consumption metrics. Timeouts and network partitions cause SDKs to retry; downstream services cannot always distinguish duplicates from new requests, which creates reconciliation friction and customer disputes. We need a solution that prevents double-charging in the common case (client quickly retries), degrades gracefully for legacy clients, and provides a clear reconciliation path for edge cases.
proposal: Introduce a short-lived 'graceful retry window' combined with provisional debits and a penalty-crediting policy. Workflow: 1) Clients may send an idempotency handle (X-Request-Dedupe-Id) or the gateway generates one on behalf of older SDKs. 2) On first ingest, the platform records a provisional debit reservation for N seconds (configurable, default 15s) tied to the dedupe id and returns a provisional token and TTL. 3) If a duplicate arrives within TTL with the same dedupe id, request is deduped and the provisional debit is not recharged. 4) If the original request times out or is cancelled, clients can call a Commit/Abort endpoint with the provisional token. 5) If the token is not committed before TTL expires, the provisional debit is automatically finalized (convert to final debit) to preserve accounting for completed-but-unconfirmed work, or released and turned into a credit depending on observed completion signals. For overloaded or rate-limited paths we use a penalty-crediting policy: when the platform performs an unavoidable double-charge due to cross-region failover or multi-hop retries, we apply an automatic credit equal to the later duplicate charge and mark an annotation for reconciliation.
api_changes: - New request header: X-Request-Dedupe-Id (client-generated UUID). - New response header: X-Provisional-Token and X-Provisional-TTL when a provisional debit is created. - New endpoints: POST /v1/usage/commit {provisional_token} and POST /v1/usage/abort {provisional_token}. - Backwards compatibility: If no dedupe id provided, gateway will optionally generate dedupe ids for supported SDK versions; older clients get a best-effort fallback (no provisional flow). - Rate-limit middleware updates: honor provisional reservations against quota checks so that duplicates do not consume additional quota while TTL active.
data_model: Flat records in the ingestion cache (Redis): keys = 'prov:{customer_id}:{dedupe_id}' -> string with fields 'provisional_token|created_at|ttl|amount|route|trace_id|origin'. TTL populated via Redis EXPIRE. Final commit entries inserted into the canonical consumption ledger (Postgres ledger table partitioned by customer). An audit log (append-only) records decisions: deduped, committed, aborted, auto-finalized, auto-credited. Reconciliation keys are simple strings and the canonical ledger entry key is the provisional_token when commit occurs.
reconciliation_process: A periodic sweep job (every 30m) will: 1) find expired provisional keys, 2) consult the request trace/span to infer whether work completed (via observability signals), 3) either finalize debit or issue a credit depending on outcome and penalty rules, and 4) emit a reconciliation event to the billing system and customer audit feed. A manual reconciliation playbook will be available for support to mark specific dedupe ids for forced refund/commit.
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: provisional_reservations_created, provisional_reservations_committed, provisional_reservations_expired, duplicates_detected_within_ttl, credits_issued_for_duplicates, auto_finalizations. Alerts: duplicate rate spike > 0.5% of requests per minute, crediting volume > $X/hour, and reconciliation sweep failure rate > 1% per run. Dashboards: per-customer duplicate incidence, TTL median, time-to-commit distribution.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind 'provisional-debits' per-customer. 2) Early rollout to internal Canary customers and SDK-instrumented teams for two weeks. 3) Enable gateway-generated dedupe ids for upgraded SDKs to capture older clients. 4) Gradual ramp to 10% of production traffic, monitor duplicates and credits, then full rollout. 5) Publish docs and SDK helpers to make X-Request-Dedupe-Id generation trivial.
acceptance_criteria: - Duplicate requests with same dedupe id within TTL must not create additional final ledger entries. - Commit endpoint correctly converts provisional reservation to final ledger entry. - Abort endpoint releases reservation and issues credit when appropriate. - Reconciliation sweep finalizes or credits expired reservations with <=1% false-positive rate in canary. - Metrics and dashboards populate within 5 minutes of traffic. - No customer receives unexplained double-billing during the canary period.
tests: Unit tests for provisional state transitions (create/commit/abort/expire), integration tests simulating multi-region retries, load test ensuring Redis TTL scale under 5k provisional ops/s, end-to-end billing test that validates ledger entries match expected charges across retries. Add fuzz tests for missing commit and delayed commit scenarios.
progress_updates: 2025-01-20: Spike completed — Redis-based provisional reservation is feasible; measured average latency 1.2ms per reservation under load.
2025-01-25: Design review with Billing and Console teams. Decided to emit audit events for every auto-credit to allow customer-facing explanations.
2025-01-29: Security review flagged need to encrypt provisional tokens at rest. Added KMS envelope support to data_model.
2025-02-02: Implementation started — gateway middleware and Redis reservation code in progress. First PR opened: feat/ingest-provisional-debits.
